_about: Every input of the Atlas v2 build, pinned (docs/atlas-v2-design.md §2.3 step 0, §2.10a, §7 Phase 0).
fetch-sources.js downloads an entry into src/<id>/ ONLY if its licence is on the accepted list and the
download's sha256 matches; a file that differs from its pin is deleted and the build stops. A source
whose publisher regenerates the file (OSM land polygons, daily) therefore goes stale deliberately:
re-pin it in a commit that says so. Every generated file under atlas/data/ copies the entries it
used into its own header, and the credits page is rendered from those headers.
Licence identifiers accepted: PD, CC0, CC-BY-3.0, CC-BY-4.0 (no conditions beyond credit);
ODbL-1.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, GPL-3.0 (share-alike: only as a data file of its own carrying the licence).
`bytes` is the Content-Length the host reported when the hash was taken; `reachable` records the
probe (node .claude/check-reach.js re-measures it — never trust a date here over a fresh run).

`blocked` holds entries that FAILED the licence check when their text was read (never fetched by ensureSource, which reads `sources` only): the finding stays on the record so the question is not re-asked from memory.

sources.licenceText: Public domain (Natural Earth terms of use); the README inside the zip adds that the supplementary European and North American rivers (not used here) are public domain too.
sources.attribution: Made with Natural Earth. Free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com.
usedBy: build-water.js (Phase 1b: rivers — the stand-in for HydroRIVERS, whose licence is not open; see `blocked`)
sources.why: Chosen 2026-10-08 when HydroRIVERS failed the licence check (below). The scale-rank edition is the plain rivers file split per scale rank, so a great river's lower course is drawn at the globe and its headwaters from LOD 1–2; it carries names, Wikidata ids and NE ids for Phase 1c. Its resolution is 1:10M (median chord 1.8 km), so rivers stop being drawn where the chords would show (§7 Phase 1b).

blocked.licence: HydroSHEDS v1 License Agreement (WWF) — NOT an accepted identifier; this entry is blocked
blocked.attribution: HydroRIVERS v1.0 © World Wildlife Fund, Inc. (2006–2013) and HydroSHEDS, CC BY 4.0. Lehner, B., Grill, G. (2013): Global river hydrography and network routing: baseline data and new approaches to study the world's large river systems. Hydrological Processes 27(15): 2171–2186.
blocked.finding: 2026-10-08: the product page says HydroRIVERS is "distributed under the same license agreement as the HydroSHEDS core products, which is included in the HydroSHEDS Technical Documentation"; that document (HydroSHEDS_TechDoc_v1_4.pdf, April 2022, Appendix A) is a WWF end-user licence: distribution only "incorporated into any Derivative Works … subject to the terms and conditions of an end user license agreement with terms that are at least as protective"; "In no event shall Licensee license or distribute the Licensed Materials as a stand-alone product"; the licensee "shall protect against unauthorized copying"; audit and record-keeping duties. Not CC BY and not an equivalent open licence (§2.10a: nothing unclear or conflicting). HydroSHEDS v2 (CC BY 4.0, hydrosheds.org/products/hydrosheds-v2) covers only the Americas as of 2026-10-08, with a global release "under a free license" announced for 2026 — re-check it before Phase 2. Phase 0 had pinned this entry as CC-BY-4.0 from memory; the sha256 and bytes are real and kept so a later session can verify a re-licensed copy.
